title: Every Airliner Gets Hit by Lightning About Once a Year

scenes.text: Every airliner gets hit by lightning about once a year.
Millions of volts, nose to tail, with 300 people inside.
Passengers see a flash and hear a bang. Then nothing happens.
The metal skin carries the current around the outside and off the wingtips, like a cage.
scenes.keywords: airplane wing tip close up flying

scenes.text: It wasn't always safe. In 1963, lightning ignited a fuel tank on a Boeing 707. 81 people died.
Every jet got new fuel vents. Nobody on a US airliner has died from lightning since.

description:
Commercial aircraft are struck by lightning roughly once a year each, and passengers usually notice only a flash and a bang.
The aluminium skin, or a conductive mesh in composite planes, carries the current around the fuselage and out through the wingtips. The last fatal lightning crash of a US airliner was Pan Am Flight 214 in December 1963, when a strike ignited fuel vapour and 81 people died; the rules changed within weeks.
Have you ever been on a plane that got hit? Comment below.

first_comment: Planes do not just get hit, they often trigger the strike themselves by flying through a charged cloud. Would you still look out of the window in a storm?
